newsitem.title: FRANCE: No Algerian plans to renew grain credits - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: No Algerian plans to renew grain credits - diplomat.

text.p: Algeria has no immediate plans to renew French or U.S.-backed credit lines for the purchase of grain and other goods, a diplomatic official at the Algerian embassy in Paris said on Wednesday.
The official, who declined to be identified, said healthy finances allowed the North African country to pay cash.
"At this stage we are ruling out renewing credit lines for the purchase of wheat or other goods," the official said.
"Currently finances are sound. So Algeria does not need credits from the Americans or the French," he added.

In early March the U.S. Agriculture Department offered $275 million in export credit guarantees for the sale of U.S. farm goods to Algeria under the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal year 1997.
The credit would cover the sale of wheat, cotton, feed grains, dairy products and vegetable oil.
Algeria, a traditional outlet for French wheat, has an outstanding Coface-guaranteed credit line for the purchase of 60,000 tonnes of French wheat, banking sources said.
However, the credit line seems poised to fall to zero in the light of recent grain sales, traders said.
The initial credit facility set up in 1995 covered the import of 1.2 million tonnes of French grain.
